Customs Act 1969: Section 13(2) of this Act provides the legal authority for the National Board of Revenue to determine import eligibility for duty-free shops.
National Board of Revenue: The board is empowered to set annual import quotas for authorized duty-free establishments operating at international airports.
Duty-Free Shop: The operational authority is granted to a specific entity in Chittagong to import a defined total value of goods for the specified fiscal year under its bonded license.
Cigarettes and Tobacco: This category of goods is included in the annual import quota allowance for the duty-free shop.
Alcoholic Beverages: The import quota includes a specific allocation for alcoholic beverages, including liquor, beer, and wine, for the fiscal year.
Cosmetic and Toiletries: These items are part of the authorized import list permitted for the duty-free shop under the current fiscal year's allocation.
Electronic: Electronics are categorized within the miscellaneous import allocation permitted for the duty-free shop.
Gift Items: Gift items are included in the permitted import categories for the duty-free shop's annual quota.

National Board of Revenue: The National Board of Revenue issues this operational order and directs the publication of the associated notification in the official gazette.
The Board instructs its system manager to publish the notification on the official website for public awareness.
Customs Commissionerate: The various regional and specialized Customs Commissionerates are formal recipients of this order to ensure administrative implementation across their respective jurisdictions.
Duty Free Shop: The management of the specified duty free shop is formally notified of the order, confirming their compliance requirements regarding the subject matter of the instruction.
